nodes.description: Public string state variable holding the current riddle question.
Address of the account allowed to change the question and stop the game.
keccak256 hash of the valid response; guards the Try() reward.
External payable function that verifies the response hash and transfers the whole contract balance to msg.sender.
Public payable initializer that sets responseHash, question and questionSender only once when responseHash is zero.
Public payable function that lets questionSender drain the contract balance.
Public payable function allowing questionSender to replace the question and response hash.
Public function allowing questionSender to transfer ownership to a new address.
Payable fallback function that accepts plain ether transfers.
msg.sender, attacker-controlled caller address used for authorization checks and as transfer recipient.
tx.origin, used in Try() to restrict calls to direct transactions, enabling phishing-style authorization bypass.
msg.sender.transfer(this.balance) inside Try(), an external value transfer performed after the hash check (reentrancy surface).
msg.sender.transfer(this.balance) inside StopGame(), external value transfer to the caller after only an address equality check.
_response string argument of Try(), hashed and compared to responseHash.
_question string argument of set_game(), written into the question state variable.
_response string argument of set_game(), hashed and stored in responseHash.
_question string argument of NewQuestion(), written into the question state variable.
_responseHash bytes32 argument of NewQuestion(), written into responseHash.
newAddress argument of newQuestioner(), stored as the new questionSender.

edges.reason: The _response parameter flows into keccak256 comparison inside Try().
The _question parameter is written to the question state variable in set_game().
The _response parameter is hashed into responseHash in set_game().
The _question parameter is written to the question state variable in NewQuestion().
The _responseHash parameter is written to responseHash in NewQuestion().
The newAddress parameter is written to questionSender in newQuestioner().
msg.sender must equal tx.origin for Try() to proceed, controlling the reward path.
tx.origin is used in the authorization check in Try(), making it dependent on the transaction origin.
Try() performs msg.sender.transfer(this.balance) once the hash and value checks pass.
msg.sender is the recipient of the balance transfer in Try(), so an attacker controls the external call target.
StopGame() performs msg.sender.transfer(this.balance) after the questionSender check.
msg.sender is the recipient of the balance transfer in StopGame().
StopGame() requires msg.sender == questionSender to authorize draining the balance.
NewQuestion() checks msg.sender == questionSender before mutating game state.
newQuestioner() checks msg.sender == questionSender before changing ownership.
msg.sender is stored into questionSender during set_game() initialization.
newQuestioner() writes newAddress into the questionSender state variable.
set_game() writes the hashed response into responseHash.
set_game() writes the supplied string into the question state variable.
set_game() writes msg.sender into questionSender.
NewQuestion() overwrites the question state variable.
NewQuestion() overwrites the responseHash state variable.
questionSender is read indirectly through state interactions gating the Try() reward path.
responseHash is compared with keccak256(_response) inside Try().
